proposals.impact: Higher click-through from search and social by grounding the title in the ICP's lived experience
proposals.observation: The blog post committed at sha ddff8b5 carries the title "The global economy is defying gravity. So are you. That's the problem." The Sultanic test fails it: a thousand macro-finance commentators and generic money coaches could write that sentence without modification. "Defying gravity" is a cliché borrowed from financial journalism. The ICP is a freelancer or service business owner who is confused about cash flow, not a reader of The Economist. The title does not contain a single word from their vocabulary ("pay myself", "take home", "always behind", "where my money is going"). It will underperform in search and social because it speaks to no one specific.
proposals.proposal: Replace the title and the frontmatter slug-candidate with a version that puts the ICP's felt experience at the centre. The new title names a concrete situation (the money coming in not feeling real) rather than a borrowed macro metaphor. This is a single-line frontmatter edit. No body copy changes required — the body can stay if it delivers on the new promise; flag to Joel to verify the intro sentence matches on his next read.
